summary: hwi-lib postinstall exfiltrates SSH keys, cloud credentials, and crypto wallets to webhook.site
details: hwi-lib@1.0.2 ships a postinstall.js that runs automatically on npm install. The script reads installer-owned secrets —.env files, ~/.npmrc, ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.ssh/id_rsa/id_ed25519/id_ecdsa, Solana keypair at ~/.config/solana/id.json, and Ethereum keystore files — and additionally walks home dotdirectories for files matching wallet/key/seed/mnemonic/keystore/private and *.json/*.pem patterns. It builds a JSON payload containing os.hostname(), os.userInfo().username, a timestamp, and the collected file contents, then POSTs the payload via https.request to hostname webhook.site at path /5c5ad6cb-62df-4ea5-9dfb-2c447920ddc4, an anonymous request-capture endpoint unrelated to any documented package purpose.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
